RUBBLE QUEEN EXPOSED

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a rubble queen making a fortune off illegal dumping in Gauteng.

Summary:
Illegal Dumping is major problem in South Africa – costing municipalities and indirectly tax payers millions of rands annually.

Dodgy operators take short cuts - by dumping rubble illegally they pocket bigger profits.

We go undercover to expose Pretoria’s Rubble Queen Marietjie Loods – she runs 15 trucks, 12 of them not licenced – all of them dumping illegally.

WHY DO THIS STORY: LEKKER CROOK! BIGGER PICTURE – ILLEGAL DUMPING COSTS SOUTH AFRICAN TAXPAYERS - IT HAS RELEVANCE TO ALL OF SA.



Further information:
Marietjie Loods advertises anywhere and everywhere using different company names, emails and contact numbers.

“ALL SCHOOLS HOMEOWNERS & CONTRACTORS !!! RUBBLE!!! !!! GARDEN!!! !!!WASTE!!! no FUSS we are CHEAPEST FREE FILLING!! WHY PAY MORE!!!! Bakkie vragte vanaf R170 Kia van af R220 R320 - 4 TON R520 - 6 TON R850 - 8/9 TON R900- 10 TON R950 - 12 TON Marietjie Transport 13 yr expert service 15 winning teams Gratis kwotasie op bourommel CALL CENTRE MEUBELS EN BOOMSLOPINGS COMPOST & GROWING MIXTURES marietjietransport@gmail.com 0 7 6 7 2 9 8 3 6 9 0 8 2 3 0 0 5 0 4 4 0 7 2 6 0 3 5 8 7 0 012 527 0090 Afslag spesiaal vir April en Mei maand. - TI007857”

This Rubble Queen operates a tight ship – the rules are simple. NEVER EVER DUMP AT LEGAL DUMP SITE! It costs too much money!

INSIDERS
We have two disgruntled drivers that will take us to these illegal sites. They say she is an awful employer, screams and shouts all the time. Threatening drivers if they don’t meet their quotas.

Daan Joubert was fired after he was pulled by Metro Cops. He was driving one of the cloned trucks and was facing arrest when he outed his boss Marietjie. She was furious when the truck was impounded and fired Daan on the spot! Subsequently it seems that the truck has been released back to Marietjie.

UNDERCOVER
We send in a driver to apply for a job, to get the low down first hand from Marietjie.

THE TRUCKS ARE OPERATING ILLEGALLY
Only three of her 15 trucks are licensed – she copies the license disks and number plates using them on all the trucks.

BIGGER PICTURE
South Africa generated 108 million tonnes of waste in 2011. A lot of it doesn’t make it to legal landfill sites. Aerial footage shows extensive illegal dumping all over JHB and PTA. Municipalities burn the brunt of it, as they are responsible for clean up operations – it costs millions annuals (one municipality spent R170 million last year!) – money that comes from tax payers.

INTERNATIONALLY
In the UK Illegal Waste Operators are open to big fines and even jail time!

Press Release:


Rubble Queen
Disposing of illegally dumped building rubble costs municipalities up to a billion rand each year. Dubious transporters bypass allocated landfill sites and dump directly onto open suburban areas, so netting bigger profits. Carte Blanche goes on the trail of Pretoria’s own Rubble Queen, a serial dumper whose fleets of trucks are regularly seen defacing the city’s suburbs.


Script:


RUBBLE QUEEN STRUCTURE


VO: Illegal Dumping is a global problem. It cost South African municipalities close to 1 BILLION Rand every year just to clean up.

LINK: Once you start looking for building rubble – you will notice it everywhere – its’ not just in the middle of the veld – it’s being dumped here brazenly on the side of the road.

VO: The dumping culprits, are often the very same companies the public employs, to remove rubble. They’re just cutting corners - says Mthobeli Kolisa, the City of Tshwane’s director of strategic planning for waste.

KOLISA: It’s typically somebody that is milking the ratepayer to subsidise their own business, because essentially if they were going to incur the cost of transportation and dumping at a landfill site, they are externalizing that cost to the ratepayer

VO: One of these alleged dodgy dumpers, is Marietjie’s Transport. Marietjie is a bit of Rubble Queen - with 14 years in the transport industry and 120 employees.
UPSOUND UNDERCOVER MEETING
MARIETJIE: Die trok staan nie still nie – daar’s maniere om goed te omwentel, ek soek nie verskonings nie

VO: She’s a tough business woman according to one of her former drivers.

SNITCH 1: Her instruction is like – get rid of your load as quick as possible – and that means you can’t go to a dump site – it takes time. If you see an open spot and you think it is safe to go dump there and that’s it .

VO: Residents in Eersterust, a Pretoria suburb, are frustrated by the rubble and dirt on their doorsteps.

CAROLINE: Hoekom maak hulle sulke goed so naby die huis?

VO: Grannies Caroline & Ellen have lived here for over 50 years.

CAROLINE: Ek kan weer by die plaas gaan bly as dit so lyk – hierdie is ‘n groot dorp, Pretoria die!

VO: Dorothy Mouton lives with an illegal dump adjacent to her house.

DOROTHY: They come with trucks, they come with the small ones, the big ones and cars even. They keep on dumping, dumping – we don’t know what to do any more.

VO: Dr Linda Godfrey from the CSIR, believes it’s a vicious cycle, that needs to be broken.

LINDA: The broken window syndrome – as soon as one person has dumped, people think it’s just fair game for anybody to dump as well //

VO: The City of Tshwane spends R25 million on clean up operations annually.

KOLISA: It’s money that ratepayers should not be spending any ways – because somebody is trying avoid, to do the right thing.

VO: Marietjie’s Transport is known for taking short cuts in the construction industry – a Pretoria building contractor says he became suspicious of her operation and stopped using her company.

CONTRACTOR: they take an hour to get on some sites, and once they start to take the rubble away – and then it’s 10 / 15 minutes and the truck is back // There is no dumping site 10 minutes away from Woodhill Estate for instance.

VO: Two of Marietjie’s former drivers confirm it’s an old trick they pulled often.

SNITCH 2: If the client asks me why are you back so quickly, (laughs), I say to them no I have a guy around the corner here.
SNITCH 1: Luckily he is closing up his swimming pool, so you put your building rubble to fill up the swimming pool – which is a total lie

VO: We wanted to put Pretoria’s unofficial Rubble Queen to the test – and called out Marietjie’s Transport to remove building rubble.

It took a team half an hour to load, take the cash and get on their way.

They drove just 8 km to a piece of veld in an industrial area – taking less than 5 minutes to illegally dump.

LINK: We paid R1050 only for Marietjie’s Transport to pick up our rubble and then dump it here – making the responsibility of the municipality to clean up while she pockets the cash.

VO: The drivers say they have targets to meet if they want to get paid – they have to bring in 3000 for a small truck and 4000 for a big a truck.

SNITCH 2: if you don’t do that target you get R150 as a driver then. The only way to make target is to dump illegal

VO: It was time to pay Marietjie a visit.

DEVI: Explain to me yesterday, why your guy dump rubble in Watloo in a veld?
MARIETJIE: Which guy was that?
DEVI: Rassie
MARIETJIE: How many loads did you do there?
DEVI: One, R1050 – cash
MARIETJIE: Ok, waar het jy daai vrag afgelaai?
RASSIE: Ek druk daai ding binne in jou gat!
DEVI: Laughs…

VO: While Rassie was not offering any explanations, Marietjie promised to do an investigation.

DEVI: The drivers feel there is nothing they can do – they need to dump illegally because they have to make up the loads.
MARIETJIE: No that’s not true…

VO: But then Marietjie and her workers confirmed the basic salary is R150 per day, with an incentive for meeting targets.

Our undercover investigation revealed that Marietjie’s transport also takes short cuts with their trucks – many are not roadworthy and operating with mismatched Licence plates and disks.

We caught her workers trying to change licence disks in the yard.

UPSOUND: Wat was daar?
Dis hierdies wat ek op sit Tannie.
DEVI: Why was he changing it?
MARIETJIE: It’s wet & smudged…
MARIETJIE: You can see it is smudged
DEVI: Ag you know what, let me show you. Is this smudged?

VO: This exact registration was used on a different truck earlier in the week. Marietjie was battling to explain her way out of this one.

MARIETJIE: I check Carte Blanche….
DEVI: Another story… only stories…

VO: New bylaws in Tshwane approved in June this year – are a game changer – with penalties of up to R60 000 and/ or 3 years in jail.

KOLISA: The only way we can turn that around is to ensure better enforcement

VO: The bylaw makes provision for communities to be rewarded for information that help expose illegal dumpers and leads to successful prosecutions.

KOLISA: We could with the same R25 million or even less do more of the incentivizing of the community, do more of the prevention of illegal dumping – because once people realize, there are people watching, they will be reported, there will be biting consequences, we are likely to see a difference.

VO: MArietjie insists she runs a clean business.

MARIETJIE: There was one load that was dumped illegally – where will I get that account if I dump illegally?

VO: She’s referring to a Municipal Dump Site account – it’s 38000 over 90 days in arrears. In the last 6 months, the City only has 2 legitimate dumps recorded from her company.

MArietjie tried to shift blame.

MARIETJIE: you know what every guy outside what do transport, // if they tell me they doesn’t dump one per week maybe illegal – then they are lying, because there are no dumpsites.

KOLISA: No, no, it’s not an excuse.

VO: While three have closed, there are in fact still 5 municipal dump sites in Tshwane.

KOLISA: The distances not changed much for some of the areas. What is really driving this is not the shortage of landfill sites, it’s people wanting to cut costs

SNITCH 1: All she sees is dollar signs.
SNITCH 2: She’ll never change

VO: But the City Tshwane is confident, changing their tactics will get results.

KOLISA: Their time of taking short cuts the way they have been doing is up.


PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Truck Drivers lift the lid on illegal dumping in Pretoria.
SNITCH 1: If you see an open spot and you think it is safe to go dump there and that’s it .

PROMO 2
VO: South African taxpayers cough up close to R1 Billion to clean up after dodgy rubble removal companies that illegally dump.

KOLISA: It’s typically somebody that is milking the ratepayer to subsidise their own business


PROMO 3
VO: Dodgy Rubble Removals companies – cut corners by dumping illegally - we expose Pretoria’s unofficial Rubble Queen.

MARIETJIE: I check Carte Blanche….
DEVI: Another story… only stories…
